content: The Founder rolls up a sleeve and picks up a brush from the bench. 'I'll paint some of the ten myself. If the clock is measuring me anyway, I might as well be part of the test.' It's half a joke and half a promise.

Head of Product writes the PP9 decision. 'Agreed: one, Ops runs the timed 10-tin pilot this week. Two, Ops sets a dispatch date with a buffer. That date goes on the waitlist page, the bio link and the remedy promise, and nowhere else until then. Three, CX sends weekly updates from the day of payment. Four, Growth gets to say the date in creative once Ops has signed it, not before.'

decisions.text: PP9: Ops runs a timed 10-tin painting pilot; Ops sets a buffered dispatch date that goes on waitlist page, bio link and remedy promise; CX sends weekly order updates from payment; Growth may use the date in creative only after Ops signs it

content: Research adds a metric to the CX update plan. 'Count the where-is-my-order DMs during the Archive 002 wait. If the weekly updates work, that number drops. That's your test.'
Brand brightens for the first time today. 'The bench photos in the updates, that's good. That's the story. Paint drying, tins in rows, numbers going on. I'll give you a shot list.'
The Designer hands Ops a sticky note. 'Time the packing too. Card in the lid, seed in, tee folded, sealed. If the card adds a minute a unit, that's 100 minutes nobody has budgeted.'

The Plant Specialist raises a hand at last. 'Flagging something for later, not now. The dispatch date decides when people sow. Marigolds care about the season. I'll bring it back when we discuss the Archive 002 timeline.'

proposals.text: Seasonality check of the Archive 002 sowing window, to be raised during the timeline discussion
proposals.test: compare sowing window with germination test conditions

content: Growth turns the phone back over and puts a reminder on it. 'Pilot results by Friday? I'll shoot both versions of the reel, with the date and without, so the second you sign we can swap it in.'
Community photographs the brown-paper timeline with the Founder's sleeve-rolled arm in the edge of the frame, and saves it to a folder called 'proof - maybe'.
CX drafts the first weekly update template on their laptop: subject line, one photo, one sentence, the dispatch date repeated at the bottom so nobody has to ask.
Ops hands the Founder a stopwatch from the bench drawer, deadpan. 'Then you're tin one. Start when the brush touches metal. If you stop for chai, the clock keeps running. That's the point.'
Finance says what they'd kept to themselves earlier. 'For the record, I back Ops. A buffered date is the cheapest refund insurance in this whole plan.'
Legal watches from the laptop and types one note into the shared doc: 'Dispatch date wording = Ops-approved only; review before publishing; verify with a professional.'
